content.title: The Cabins at Augusta National Golf Course
content.text: The Cabins at Augusta National Augusta National has 10 cabins that are placed along its grounds. Seven of these are placed near the 10th fairway and the Par 3 course. Three of these cabins, the Eisenhower, Butler, and Roberts Cabins are separated, and the Eisenhower and Butler cabins are the most famous cabins. Eisenhower Cabin Constructed in 1953, the Eisenhower Cabin was designed by local architects in conjunction with the secret service to ensure that the president at the time, Dwight D. Eisenhower, would be safe during his vacations in Augusta. The cabin is located near Augusta’s 10th tee and includes three stores and seven bedrooms. Butler Cabin Named after Thomas B. Butler, a former Augusta National club member, the Butler Cabin was built in 1964 for lodging. In 1965, however, it was used as the broadcast headquarters by CBS. The Butler Cabin is located between the main clubhouse and the Par 3 Course. Aside from the basement where the CBS broadcasted the tournament, the interior of the cabin remains a mystery, a secret that no Augusta National club member has revealed. Can I rent one of the cabins at Augusta National? Unless you are a club member or related to one in some way, the answer is NO, you cannot rent one of the cabins at Augusta National. The cabins are only used by club members and their families. Also, guests of official club members can find lodging in one of the cabins while vising the course.
